The core challenge is evaluating millions of candidate features cheaply while avoiding overfitting. OpenFE uses FeatureBoost to estimate incremental gains via residual fitting, which is computationally cheaper than full retraining. Two-stage pruning then removes redundant features. This approach trades off exhaustive search optimality for linearithmic complexity, making it scalable. However, the static split assumption fails for time-series sports data where temporal order matters, introducing lookahead bias. To adapt, we must incorporate temporal validation windows and ensure feature lags respect causality.
